kandidaty.tekst:
- Added auto mode for Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude apps gateway; interactive sessions with no permission mode start in it
- Added "onFailure": "block" for mcp_tool hooks, as for command and HTTP hooks: a hook whose call fails blocks the action
- Added a warning when a message from a session that skips permission prompts may be held and dropped by a cloud session
- Added a notice in /status and claude doctor when an OpenTelemetry exporter has no endpoint and its data would likely be lost
- Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_DEFERRED_TOOL_RESUME, which lets a host stop claude -p --resume and --continue from running a tool call that a hook deferred
- Added support for apps that embed Claude Code to switch on the policy plugin's allowManagedModsOnly option; an admin's managed settings still win
- Added a startup warning to the Claude apps gateway when a policy's maxEffortLevel is not a valid effort level
- Self-hosted runner: Added --repository-folder to name the folder that sessions use for a repository at --capacity 1, in place of its path under the base folder, which can't be a symbolic link
- Self-hosted runner: Added a start-up warning when the host's settings.json sets a default permission mode that sessions ignore
- Self-hosted runner: Added --hook-label to claude self-hosted-runner orchestrator, to hand chosen session labels to the spawn-runner hook
- Self-hosted runner: Added --metadata key=value to claude --environment, to label a session for the spawn-runner hook
- Self-hosted runner: Added claude_code_self_hosted_orchestrator_session_queue_wait_by_reason_seconds to the orchestrator's /metrics, so a re-opened session's wait can be told from a new one's
- Self-hosted runner: Added an orchestrator metric, claude_code_self_hosted_orchestrator_sessions_given_up_total, that counts by cause how often Anthropic gave up starting a runner for a session
- [VSCode] Added a notice when a message from another session is held, with a link to the settings file that can allow it
- Changed plan mode and Bash prompts for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 on third-party providers to use and offer auto mode, as on newer models; disableAutoMode turns both off
- Changed Code Mode to no longer run UserPromptSubmit hooks, managed ones included, on scripts' output; to redact that output, use a PostToolUse hook with updatedToolOutput
- Changed /code-review on most models to report only bugs and CLAUDE.md violations; run /simplify for reuse, simplification and efficiency cleanups
- Changed /code-review to mark each finding Important, Pre-existing or Nit on most models, and to end each summary with a suggested fix; a clean review's list now reads "Code review found no issues."
- Changed deniedMcpServers entries of the form claude.ai <name> to apply to that connector in cloud and self-hosted runner sessions too
- Changed managed PostToolUse hooks to no longer fire for calls refused before they ran: no log e

kandidaty.tekst:
OpenAI shipped GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol today, two days before Anthropic’s expected first trading day. In Artificial Analysis’ tests, Sol ties September’s Astra at about 15% of the cost per task. New Astra scores 62 on the Intelligence Index, just behind Fable 5.2 at 65. Net net, Anthropic still owns the world’s best model, but OpenAI owns the world’s most efficient models in terms of intelligence per $.

What’s more unusual about this launch is the STRONGLY negative influencer feedback…

which prompted a defensive response…

View post on X ↗

We think that some of this is overreacting and normal influencer tendency to either have everything be 🤯🤯🤯 or the literal WORST.MODEL.EVER, BUT also that some of the criticisms are valid, and the RL artefacts are noticeable and downright bizarre (don’t even get us started about the terrible launch video). However, we still use it to automate our work and that’s all that matters in the end.

Great ship, but Anthropic’s IPO is unaffected and that will be probably the headline of the week/year/decade (until OpenAI IPO’s….)

kandidaty.zagolovok: We're sharing new data on how AI is changing research at OpenAI. We find researchers' AI use continues to rise exponenti
kandidaty.tekst:
@OpenAI: We're sharing new data on how AI is changing research at OpenAI.

We find researchers' AI use continues to rise exponentially, and agents are completing longer tasks, but human involvement remains central in research. Researchers are also spending more time on safety and alignment, with human effort in these areas growing faster than in any other individual research area.

This report aims to increase transparency around research acceleration and inform the governance of increasingly capable AI. We believe that AI labs should be required to track and publicly report indicators of recursive self-improvement (RSI): the process by which AI accelerates the development of future AI systems. 

Our hope is that this expanded report will help sustain and advance shared measurement norms across the industry.

https://openai.com/index/research-acceleration-jagged-frontier/

kandidaty.zagolovok: We’re sharing how we approach safety at every stage of a model’s lifecycle, from early research to internal use to publi
kandidaty.tekst:
@OpenAI: We’re sharing how we approach safety at every stage of a model’s lifecycle, from early research to internal use to public deployment.

Цитирует @kaicathyc: A lot has happened in the past couple months, to say the least.

Today we are sharing a recap of what it takes to move a frontier model from training to internal use to public release. As model capabilities rise, so do the safety and alignment standards required to move forward to the next stage.

To meet these standards, we rely on four layers of protection:
1. Model alignment: train models to reliably act as intended and respect human oversight.
2. Security and sandboxing: restrict what models can access and affect.
3. Blocking safeguards: stop harmful or unauthorized actions before they happen.
4. Monitoring and response: detect concerning behavior and intervene.

The post brings together efforts from across the company, with links to recent research, technical work, and incident reports we’ve published. This is the baseline operational discipline we owe people as we continue training and deploying models - necessary work, but not a solution to alignment in the limit. There’s a lot more to do, and will continue keeping you informed as the thinking and work evolves. 🏗️

https://openai.com/index/managing-frontier-ai-risk/

kandidaty.zagolovok: PromptArmor has released FrontierBreach, a benchmark of how often AI agents at work can be misled by hidden instructions
kandidaty.tekst:
@testingcatalog: PromptArmor has released FrontierBreach, a benchmark of how often AI agents at work can be misled by hidden instructions.

Attackers can hide an invisible line in an email or document, and agents may try to follow it, sending data out or running the attacker's code.

> Across 21 AI models, these hidden attacks worked on 34.9% of PromptArmor's tests.

> PromptArmor breached every frontier model it tested, from Gemini Argon at 4.3% to Muse Wonder at 15.2%, with Grok 4.5 falling for 91.4% of the attacks.

> Attacks hidden inside agent skills also worked in 45.5% of the tests.

Цитирует @PromptArmor: Today we’re releasing FrontierBreach, a new standard for attack success rate on agentic workflows in the enterprise. 

Existing benchmarks systematically underrepresent the security risks facing modern AI agents. 

FrontierBreach reflects attack scenarios on realistic enterprise workflows, while using sophisticated attack chains that result in cyber consequences (ransomware, data exfiltration, phishing, etc).
